course: There is not any positive aspect to this course other than it is being the end of all these things. I could not find any benefit from either the course or the instructors. I realized that I was delusional for having high hopes that I will graduate with a fully developed project. But, I do not believe that a project can reach its full potential without progressive feedback. This course was supposed to be a guide for our graduation project that we would feel very proud of, but rather it was some sort of a series of sessions that never helped us through the production. Our instructors greatly failed at giving us the instructions every single time in every single case. There was certainly no clarity for us on what to and how to deliver. The course was unorganized, inconsistent, and the instructors seemed unbothered and unwilling. I think such an important course like this should be given by instructors who are willing and caring for the sake of all the students and the projects. I had thought VCP would be about receiving feedbacks and making progress, while it was more like a chit-chat session for me. Some of the instructors were clearly uninterested in some projects. The creative projects couldn't even get half of the feedback that communication projects got. While our (section 2) instructor gave feedback to everyone, the other instructors of other sections never even bothered to listen to our presentations. I can easily count the number of feedback that we received through approximately 30 weeks. I have been thinking that I was in film and media school, but this course made me reconsider where we stand in COMD as people who are eager to work in filmmaking. Clearly, this course failed to provide us any support and it mainly forced us to get discouraged about our projects (not because of negative feedback, because of “no feedback”). Sadly, I feel like I have wasted 4 years thanks to this unsatisfactory VCP course that made me question my whole experience in COMD.
